title: Airhelp v SAS (Case C-28/20), 23 March 2021
excerpt: strike action which is entered into upon a call by a trade union of the staff of an operating air carrier, in compliance with the conditions laid down by national legislation, in particular the notice period imposed by it, which is intended to assert the demands of that carrier’s workers and which is followed by a category of staff essential for operating a flight does not fall within the concept of an ‘extraordinary circumstance’
summary: A lawful strike by the carrier's own staff, called by their union, is not an extraordinary circumstance.
